data.title: A talk on archaeology at the school in Dolné Orešany
data.excerpt: Public outreach is an important part of heritage work and of archaeology, yet until recently I had never given a talk intended only for children. At the school in Dolné Orešany the audience even grew: the nursery-school children were so taken by the programme they could see through the fence that their teachers brought them along.
data.metaTitle: A talk on archaeology for children in Dolné Orešany
data.metaDescription: An outreach talk on archaeology prepared for children at the primary and nursery school in Dolné Orešany — an important part of heritage protection work.

mediaTexts.alt: A speaker in front of a group of children sitting on the grass in the school grounds

children.text: I consider public outreach an important part of heritage work and of archaeology. I devote a great deal of effort to it, and the positive results encourage me to carry on with such work. I am also very glad when more and more archaeologists become involved in it. Until recently, however, I had never given a talk intended only for children, and so I was delighted that I would at last be visiting a primary school at its own invitation. I had been informed that all the year groups would attend, so I prepared my presentation for a wide age range. In the end, however, most of the pupils of the lower primary classes had another programme, but they were “stood in for” by the children from the nursery school, whose teachers joined them to the audience because the programme they could see through the fence interested them so much.

I organised the talk together with Lukáš, a member of the Hradiská civic association. The spot where we set up was ideal, because it offered a view of several fortifications. The talk was divided into chapters: “What archaeology is”, “What archaeological heritage is” and “What monuments are”. The children thus learned what the word archaeology means, what we study, what archaeology brings us, what methods, procedures, tools and equipment we use, what archaeological finds, features and sites are, what to do when you make a find, what websites and groups about archaeology there are on the internet, where to find heritage officers, what movable and immovable monuments they have in their village and in the nearby town, and so on. Lukáš presented the important archaeological sites in the cadastral area of the village and explained why they need to be protected. At the end the children could look at publications on archaeology, at photographs and drawings of finds made in their own cadastral area, handle finds from various periods and of various materials, take information leaflets and try out the tools and equipment used in excavations, including the most modern kind.

children.text: If you think that the primary school you attended, or the one your children attended or attend, might be interested in a talk like this, tell them about us. If they get in touch, I will give the talk at your school myself, or — if it is in a more distant region — one of my colleagues will.
M. Sládok (archaeologist of the Regional Monuments Board in Trnava)
